correctness.rationale: For all \(m\ge2\) and \(1\le r<m\), each Gold derivative has the affine kernel \(a\mathbb F_{2^h}\) of cardinality \(K\). The ambiguity restricted to a nonempty derivative fiber is an additive character, and exactly \(q/K\) first-coordinate frequencies survive for every admissible \((a,c,d)\). At zero translation, the radical equation \(d^{2^r}t^{2^{2r}}+dt=0\) gives the radical cardinalities \(K\) in the odd-index branch and \(K^2\) versus \(1\) in the even-index branch, with explicitly counted coefficient classes. Quadratic Walsh orthogonality gives all amplitudes and supports; full Weyl diagonalization gives the normalized lifting singular values \(q|A_g|\). The proof establishes the complete histogram independently of finite tests. Packaged exhaustive integer Walsh checks for field orders 4, 8, 16 and 32, and a direct 256-by-256 projector-Gram eigenvalue check for field order 4, passed.

value.rationale: Full spectral support and conditioning of a Gabor projector measurement system are intrinsic complex-matrix identifiability and stability invariants. The theorem determines them exactly for all binary Gold graph exponents and extension-field degrees. The parity of \(m/\gcd(m,r)\) separates two different zero-translation Walsh strata with explicit arithmetic multiplicities, while the positive-spectrum condition number is uniformly \(q/K\). This classification goes beyond restating the well-known derivative uniformity or Fourier-extension fourth-moment identity, and may be relevant to later phase-retrieval window analysis; no unproved nonlinear recovery guarantee is claimed.
